newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - H&Q sees Chips overvalued.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - H&Q sees Chips overvalued.

text.p: Hambrecht & Quist analyst Robert Chaplinsky reaffirmed his buy rating on Chips and Technologies Inc but said he was concerned the graphics chip maker's shares had become overpriced.
Analysts said Chaplinsky's comments were behind the sharp fall in Chips and Technologies shares Monday.
The stock was off 3 to 20-7/8 late Monday afternoon after falling as three points earlier in the day. Chips was among the most actively traded stocks on Nasdaq.
Chaplinsky said he made no change in earnings estimates for Chips, and that its "near-term fundamentals remain solid."

"(Chips and Technologies) has reached a point of valution that still has the potential to move north, but I just think it's moved a lot already," the Hambrecht analyst said in a phone interview. "It has far exceeded my price target."
The analyst said he has not changed his financial models or rating on the company, a top supplier of personal computer graphics accelerator chips. He did not set a new price target.

"I just thought that at 23 or 24 it was reaching its all time high in terms of valuation. For better appreciation, I suggested (investors) look at a stock like ESS Technology Inc," he said, referring to ESS, a PC audio chip maker.
The analyst said he maintained his current earnings estimate for the fiscal year ending in June of $1.08 per share, on a fully taxed basis.

In addition to valuation, Chaplinsky said he was concerned about Chips' position as the leading supplier of graphics chips for notebook computers, a dominance he expects to come under competitive attack in the upcoming year.
Among the rivals expected to offer competing products are S3 Inc, Cirrus Logic Inc, Trident Microsystems Inc along with several emerging private companies which he declined to name.

"Next year the competitve landscape gets very interesting," he said. "It's too early to predict if they will be successful, but just the fact that they are out there marketing their products may put some pressure on the stock," Chaplinsky said, referring to the company and its rivals.
While declining to set a new price target, Chaplinsky noted on the heels of its sell-off Monday that, "(Chips and Tech) is obviously a little more attractive today."
"Basically I said with its current valution it ran up pretty fast here," Chaplinsky said of his morning comments.
The Hambrecht analyst had set a price target of $16 when he initiated Chips and Tech with a buy rating in August. The stock traded at $10 when he issued the buy rating, he noted.
"The stock is up 150 percent since we recommended it in August," he said.

Chaplinsky comments came in the context of a discussion of several chip makers, including Intel Corp, which he sees as running with full cylinders" and having "strong fundamentals." He said his postive outlook on ESS stock was
based on its growth opportunity in the video compact disc market. ESS stock was off 5/8 at 19-3/4 late Monday.
